format_reason: New standalone museum painting; natural approved Gacrux not verified as free/available, and format remains non-narrated rather than substituting robotic speech.

candidates_considered.title: The Sea of Ice
candidates_considered.reason: Selected: extraordinary angular glacier, nearly hidden ship, first-frame mystery, museum-verified 1820–21 Elbe studies and clean Commons PD-Art source.

candidates_considered.title: The Nightmare
candidates_considered.reason: Visually compelling but museum reproduction rights require more care and image has sensitive sexualized incubus symbolism.

candidates_considered.title: The Fighting Temeraire
candidates_considered.reason: Excellent museum story and glowing light, but painting is already present in older ArtVision batch profiles and less surprising than the ice wreck.

sea_of_ice.story: A nearly invisible ship becomes the emotional hook; monumental broken ice dwarfs it. The painting's harsh planes become a quiet reflection on the limits of human ambition. Finish with an opaque, perfectly complete canvas, not a generic zoom loop.

scenes.intent: Open on the almost-hidden broken ship on the right, so viewers discover the painting's secret first
Reveal the angular peak of crushed ice and the disproportionate scale of the landscape
Hold on the dark blue and green foreground slabs where ice resembles shattered stone
Shift to the distant left glacier and the cold horizon for an essential breath
Return to the ship's tiny hull trapped between two jagged walls of ice
Examine pale green light along the angled front ice plates
Study the monumental upward thrust of the central jagged ice tower
Allow stillness in the sky and distant frozen sea without decorative motion
Return to the entire mountain of ice before the closing full-canvas reveal
Finish on the complete genuine painting centered on a fully opaque dark matte
